category.label: openers and frames
category.description: Openers and frames that delay the point.

source: avoid-ai-writing by Conor Bronsdon (MIT) and Ryan Yannelli's house rules

patterns.regex: ^(?:But )?(?:what|so why|why) (?:does this mean|should you care|does (?:it|this) matter)\b
patterns.show: `What does this mean`, `So why should you care`, `Why does it matter` as an opener

patterns.regex: ^\s*(?:picture this|run the numbers|think about it|consider this)[.:]
patterns.show: `Picture this.`, `Run the numbers.`, `Think about it.`, `Consider this:` as a line-initial fragment

patterns.fix: drop the count, lead with the finding
patterns.show: `Three key takeaways`, `5 things to know`, `Four reasons`, `10 ways`, `Six tips` (line-initial)

patterns.regex: ^\s*(?:let me (?:think|break this down|walk through this) step by step|here['’]s my thought process|to approach this systematically|breaking this down:)
patterns.show: `Let me think step by step`, `Let me break this down step by step`, `Let me walk through this step by step`, `Here's my thought process`, `To approach this systematically`, `Breaking this down:`

patterns.fix: name it in a plain sentence
patterns.show: `Enter Redis.` and the rest of the reveal form

patterns.phrase: (?:have you )?ever wondered|what if I told you

patterns.show: `Imagine a world where`, `Picture a future in which`, `Envision a scenario where`

patterns.opening: you're asking about|to answer your question|the question of whether
patterns.show: `You're asking about`, `To answer your question`, `The question of whether` (sentence-initial)
